meta.policy: Every value is either stated by an official source or computed by the published formula from such values. Commercial fees are never filled in.

scenarios.A: own already-taxed money: PRC conversion tax 0%, US tax on transfer 0%
scenarios.B: whole amount treated as PRC comprehensive income of a resident with no other income
scenarios.C: whole amount treated as PRC 20% flat-category income; US residual after credit
scenarios.D: statutory fine range if a prohibited channel were used (Decree 532 Arts. 39-45)

methods.name: Documented after-tax RMB income → bank conversion → SWIFT wire
methods.verified_limit: No annual USD cap is stated for a non-domestic individual's conversion of lawful current-account income; the bank reviews authenticity. The USD 50,000 annual total in Art. 2 is expressly tied to domestic individuals' purchases and to all individuals' FX sales.
methods.verified_cost: 0% PRC tax on the conversion itself (S04 Art. 2 lists no such category); the tax is on the underlying income.
methods.note: This is the route the research points to first for documented, already-taxed money.

methods.name: Re-conversion of unused RMB from an earlier FX conversion (original exchange memo)
methods.verified_limit: Bounded by the amount on the original memo and the 24-month validity window.
methods.verified_cost: 0% tax: this is a return of your own previously converted principal, not new income.
methods.note: Amounts on the memo are personal facts and are not published anywhere; left unverified.

methods.name: Walk-in small-amount re-conversion with ID only
methods.verified_limit: USD 500 per day; USD 1,000 per day at port outlets; per person.
methods.verified_cost: 0% tax. Commercial spread/fee unverified.
methods.note: A safety valve, not a repatriation plan.

methods.name: Remit an existing FX savings-account balance abroad
methods.verified_limit: Art. 15(1) states no annual amount for a non-domestic individual's outward remittance from an FX savings account. (Domestic individuals are handled under Art. 14: USD 50,000/day with ID, above that with authenticity documents.)
methods.verified_cost: 0% PRC tax; 0% US tax on moving your own funds.
methods.note: The cheapest lawful path when it applies: no conversion spread, because no conversion is needed.

methods.name: Overseas ATM cash withdrawals with a PRC bank card
methods.verified_limit: RMB 100,000 equivalent per individual per civil year across all cards; RMB 10,000 equivalent per card per day. Exceeding the annual cap suspends overseas cash withdrawal for the current and the following year.
methods.verified_cost: 0% tax. Commercial: issuer conversion rate, out-of-network ATM surcharges - unverified.
methods.note: Also note the US CMIR rule if physical cash crosses the border (S14).

methods.name: Overseas merchant / POS spending with a PRC card
methods.verified_limit: No published fixed amount; spending must be genuine personal consumption and the card's own limit applies.
methods.verified_cost: 0% tax. Not a way to obtain USD cash for other purposes.
methods.note: Counts as a legitimate consumption channel only.

methods.name: Carry physical cash across the border
methods.verified_limit: PRC declaration limits: not re-verified in this session (prior sessions cited the GACC passenger guide, S22). US side verified: more than USD 10,000 must be reported on FinCEN Form 105, aggregated across a family or group.
methods.verified_cost: 0% tax if declared. Seizure risk if not declared (S14).
methods.note: A last resort for small amounts.

methods.name: Sale of PRC real estate by a foreign individual, then remit after-tax proceeds
methods.verified_limit: No fixed cap; documentation-driven. Real-estate FX handling is governed by the separate property rules referenced in S02 Art. 21.
methods.verified_cost: PRC IIT on the transfer gain at 20% (S04 Art. 3(3)); 0% tax on the act of conversion.
methods.note: The 'conversion penalty' people feel is usually this 20% on the gain, already owed before any conversion.

methods.name: Inheritance outbound transfer (继承财产转移)
methods.verified_limit: Procedure-based; the amount follows the estate documents. The 2004 notice is cited from a prior session (S17) and not re-fetched here.
methods.verified_cost: PRC IIT treatment of inherited assets depends on the asset and the estate's tax position; not quantified here.
methods.note: Documentation and approvals, not a tax rate, are the binding constraint.

methods.name: Emigrant personal-asset transfer (移民财产转移) — former PRC residents only
methods.verified_limit: Procedure-based, one-time in principle; tied to assets held before emigration and to the household-registration cancellation.
methods.verified_cost: PRC taxes on the underlying assets as applicable; 0% on conversion.
methods.note: Not available to a US citizen who never emigrated from mainland China.

methods.name: PRC-citizen USD 50,000/year facilitated FX purchase quota
methods.verified_limit: USD 50,000 equivalent per person per calendar year (S02 Art. 2; S01 Art. 9).
methods.verified_cost: 0% tax on the purchase itself.
methods.note: S11 Art. 52(2) defines 境内个人 as including foreigners resident in China for one full year, which conflicts with the narrower reading used by an earlier session. Flagged, not resolved.

methods.name: Transfer between FX savings accounts of immediate relatives
methods.verified_limit: Domestic FX-account transfers only; a transfer between a domestic and a non-domestic individual's account is treated as a cross-border transaction (S02 Art. 28(3)).
methods.verified_cost: 0% tax on the transfer; the receiving relative's own quota and tax position then apply.
methods.note: Lawful for genuine family support; unlawful if used to evade limits.

methods.name: PRC employer pays salary directly to your US account
methods.verified_limit: No personal cap; the employer's remittance rules and the tax record filing apply.
methods.verified_cost: PRC IIT withheld at source (3%-45% comprehensive, S04); 0% on the remittance.

methods.name: Dividends / profit repatriation from a PRC company you own
methods.verified_limit: No personal cap; corporate tax and withholding must be settled first.
methods.verified_cost: PRC withholding on dividends at the 20% statutory flat rate (S04 Art. 3(3)); a treaty rate may reduce this but was not re-verified here (F04).
methods.note: Corporate-level tax is a separate, earlier layer.

methods.name: Equity transfer or company liquidation proceeds
methods.verified_limit: No fixed cap; the taxable gain and approvals drive the timing.
methods.verified_cost: PRC IIT on the transfer gain at 20% (S04 Art. 3(3)); 0% on conversion.

methods.name: Genuine cross-border service fees, royalties or IP licensing
methods.verified_limit: No cap; arm's-length pricing and genuine delivery are required.
methods.verified_cost: PRC withholding on royalties at the 20% statutory flat rate (S04); VAT may also apply (not re-verified).

methods.name: Individual FX settlement account / licensed payment institutions
methods.verified_limit: Requires foreign-trade registration or a licensed institution; not a personal remittance channel.
methods.verified_cost: 0% tax on conversion; business income tax applies to the underlying profit.

methods.name: Splitting amounts across friends' or relatives' USD 50,000 quotas (smurfing)
methods.verified_limit: Not lawful — no limit applies because the channel itself is prohibited.
methods.verified_cost: Not a cost: a penalty. Up to 30% of the amount, or 30%-100% if serious, plus confiscation and possible criminal liability (S11 Arts. 39-45).
methods.note: S01 Art. 7; S02 Art. 28/13; S03 Art. I

methods.name: Underground banks and informal onshore/offshore RMB-USD swaps (对敲)
methods.verified_limit: Not lawful — no limit applies because the channel itself is prohibited.
methods.verified_cost: Not a cost: a penalty. Up to 30%, or 30%-100% if serious, plus confiscation (S11 Art. 45).

methods.name: Crypto / stablecoin OTC bridge
methods.verified_limit: Not lawful — no limit applies because the channel itself is prohibited.
methods.verified_cost: Not a cost: a penalty. Virtual-currency business activity is prohibited; FX and criminal exposure also apply. Not re-fetched here.

methods.name: Fabricated or over-invoiced trade / consulting contracts
methods.verified_limit: Not lawful — no limit applies because the channel itself is prohibited.
methods.verified_cost: Not a cost: a penalty. Illegal FX arbitrage: up to 30%, or 30%-100% if serious (S11 Art. 40).

methods.name: Overseas POS cash-out, or borrowing other people's bank cards
methods.verified_limit: Not lawful — no limit applies because the channel itself is prohibited.
methods.verified_cost: Not a cost: a penalty. Card use is suspended and fines follow; borrowing or lending cards to evade the rules is expressly prohibited (S03).

sources.title: Administrative Rules on Individual's Foreign Exchange (PBOC Decree [2006] No.3, English)
sources.evidence: Art. 9 imposes an annual limit on an individual's FX sales and on domestic individuals' FX purchases. Art. 13: a non-domestic individual may convert legitimate RMB current-account income and remit abroad with valid ID and relevant documents. Art. 7 prohibits evading limits by splitting amounts or fabricating vouchers.

sources.title: Implementing Rules for the Administrative Rules on Individual's Foreign Exchange (汇发[2007]1号), 2024 republication with amendments
sources.evidence: Art. 2: annual total of USD 50,000 equivalent per person per year for individual FX sales and domestic individuals' FX purchases. Art. 13(1): non-domestic individual converting lawful current-account RMB income presents ID plus supporting documents including tax vouchers (含税务凭证). Art. 13(2): unused RMB from an original conversion may be re-converted against the original exchange memo, valid 24 months; same-day amounts of USD 500 or less (USD 1,000 or less at pre-departure port outlets) need only ID. Art. 15(1): a non-domestic individual remitting FX abroad from an FX savings account presents valid ID. Art. 20: emigration asset transfer and foreign inheritance transfer follow the separate 2004 rules. Footnote: Art. 39 was repealed by 汇发[2023]8号.

sources.title: Circular on Regulating Large-sum Overseas Cash Withdrawals with Bank Cards (汇发[2017]29号, English)
sources.evidence: Withdrawals with a domestic bank card shall not exceed the equivalent of RMB 100,000 in every civil year per individual across all cards; excess triggers a ban on overseas cash withdrawal in the current and the second year. Per-card daily ceiling adjusted from USD 1,000 to RMB 10,000; RMB cards remain at RMB 10,000 per card per day. Borrowing or lending cards to evade the rule is prohibited. Effective 1 January 2018.

sources.title: Individual Income Tax Law of the PRC (English translation, 2018 amendment)
sources.evidence: Art. 2 lists the nine taxable income categories; there is no category for 'converting your own money'. Art. 3: comprehensive income 3%-45%; business income 5%-35%; interest/dividends, asset leasing, asset transfer and incidental income a flat 20%. Art. 6: resident comprehensive income deducts RMB 60,000 per year; non-resident wages deduct RMB 5,000 per month. Art. 16: foreign-currency income is converted at the central parity rate. The rate schedules themselves are published as images on this page.

sources.title: 个人所得税税率表 (comprehensive income rate schedule, official text)
sources.note: Chinese-language official text; used because S04's schedule is an image.

sources.title: 26 U.S.C. §988 — Treatment of certain foreign currency transactions
sources.evidence: §988(a)(1)(A): foreign currency gain or loss on a §988 transaction is computed separately and treated as ORDINARY income or loss. §988(e)(1): the section does not apply to a §988 transaction entered into by an individual which is a personal transaction. §988(e)(2): on disposition of nonfunctional currency in a personal transaction no gain is recognized by reason of exchange-rate changes, unless the gain would exceed $200.

sources.title: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 — 2026 inflation-adjusted amounts
sources.evidence: 2026 single-filer brackets (10% to $12,400; 12% to $50,400; 22% to $105,700; 24% to $201,775; 32% to $256,225; 35% to $640,600; 37% above). 2026 standard deduction single $16,100. Foreign earned income exclusion $132,900. Gift annual exclusion $19,000. §6039F large-gift reporting threshold from foreign corporations/partnerships $20,573.

sources.title: Report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts (FBAR)
sources.locator: Who must file; When to file
sources.evidence: A U.S. person must file FinCEN Form 114 if the aggregate value of foreign financial accounts exceeded $10,000 at any time during the calendar year, whether or not the account produced taxable income. Due 15 April with an automatic extension to 15 October.

sources.title: Do I need to file Form 8938?
sources.evidence: Unmarried taxpayer living in the US: more than $50,000 on the last day of the year or more than $75,000 at any time. Taxpayer living abroad filing a non-joint return: more than $200,000 on the last day or $300,000 at any time; joint $400,000 / $600,000.

sources.title: Gifts from foreign person (Form 3520 Part IV)
sources.evidence: A foreign gift or bequest is an amount the recipient treats as a gift or bequest and EXCLUDES FROM GROSS INCOME. Reporting on Form 3520 Part IV is required when aggregate gifts from a nonresident alien or foreign estate exceed $100,000 in the year; for foreign corporations/partnerships the threshold is $20,116 (2025) and $20,573 (2026). Penalties are under IRC §6039F(c) absent reasonable cause.

sources.title: Regulations of the PRC on Foreign Exchange Administration (State Council Decree No. 532)
sources.evidence: Art. 39 (evading FX controls by moving domestic FX or capital abroad): fine up to 30% of the amount; if serious, 30% up to the equivalent of the amount; criminal liability possible. Art. 40 (illegal FX arbitrage, including fraudulent purchase with false or invalid documents): same 30% / 30%-100% scale. Art. 42 (breaching cash-carry rules): warning and fine up to 20%. Art. 45 (private or disguised FX trading): warning, confiscation, up to 30%, or 30%-100% if serious. Art. 48: individuals up to RMB 50,000 for, among other things, failing to submit valid documents. Art. 52(2) defines 境内个人 as Chinese citizens AND foreigners who have continuously resided in China for one full year (diplomats excluded).

sources.title: RMB central parity rate announcement, 6 November 2026
sources.evidence: Interbank central parity on 2026-11-06: USD 1 = CNY 6.7168. Used only to express RMB statutory thresholds in USD; the rate changes daily.

sources.title: Foreign Tax Credit
sources.evidence: A credit may be claimed only for foreign taxes imposed on income that is also subject to US tax; no credit is allowed for taxes on income excluded from US gross income (for example under the foreign earned income exclusion); where a treaty reduces the foreign tax, only the reduced amount qualifies.

sources.authority: U.S. Customs and Border Protection / FinCEN
sources.title: Money and Other Monetary Instruments (FinCEN Form 105, CMIR)
sources.evidence: Anyone who brings, sends or receives more than $10,000 in currency or monetary instruments at one time into or out of the United States must report it; the threshold applies to the total carried by a family or group, not per person. Failure risks forfeiture and seizure plus civil or criminal penalties.

sources.title: Instructions for Form 3520 (12/2025)
sources.locator: When and where to file; Penalties
sources.evidence: Form 3520 is due the 15th day of the 4th month after the tax year end, extended to the 15th day of the 10th month; a penalties section covers §6677, §6039F and §6662(j). The individual penalty percentages are not reproduced here.

flagged.title: Bank spread, cable fees and intermediary charges are not published anywhere official
flagged.detail: Every all-in dollar figure on this site excludes the commercial layer. No PRC or US regulator publishes a bank's customer spread or wire fee, so those cells are blank by design. Obtain an executable quote from your own bank and enter it in the calculator.
flagged.action: Ask the bank for the all-in price in writing: spread versus the central parity, outgoing fee, intermediary lift, and the US receiving fee.

flagged.title: Who counts as a 境内个人? Two official texts point different ways
flagged.detail: Two official texts point different ways. State Council Decree 532 Art. 52(2) defines 境内个人 as Chinese citizens AND foreigners who have continuously resided in China for one full year; an earlier session's portal asserted flatly that the USD 50,000 quota is never available to a US passport holder. The implementing rules do not restate the definition. Note the direction of the risk: being classified as 境内个人 would IMPOSE the USD 50,000 annual cap on purchases rather than remove it, whereas the Art. 13 documented route for a non-domestic individual states no dollar cap. So the bank's classification decision changes whether a large balance can move in one cycle or needs eight years.
flagged.action: Ask the specific bank, in writing, which category it will record you under, and keep that answer.

flagged.title: Resident vs non-resident IIT computation changes the answer
flagged.detail: The computed PRC figures assume resident status: annual brackets with a RMB 60,000 deduction. A non-resident is computed monthly with a RMB 5,000 deduction and a monthly-converted schedule (S04 Art. 2 and 6(2)). No personal residency facts were supplied, so the resident case is used and labelled.
flagged.action: If you spent fewer than 183 days in China in each tax year concerned, the non-resident computation may apply.

flagged.title: Treaty 10% cap on dividends, interest and royalties
flagged.detail: An earlier session reported a 10% treaty maximum under Articles 9-11 and warned that only the treaty-reduced tax is creditable. The IRS page on the credit supports the second half (S13). The treaty text itself was not re-fetched in this session, so no computed cell relies on the 10% rate; the 20% statutory rate is used.
flagged.action: Confirm the article and the limitation-on-benefits wording before relying on a treaty rate.

flagged.title: Whether the PRC tax on the income has already been paid
flagged.detail: This single fact decides whether the cost is 0% or 3%-45%. A 完税证明 or the withholding records settle it. Nothing in the repository can infer it.
flagged.action: Locate the tax payment certificate or the employer's withholding records before visiting the bank.

flagged.title: Cost basis and acquisition date are unknown
flagged.detail: The PRC 20% on an asset transfer applies to the gain, and the US §988 result depends on the USD basis at acquisition. Neither is known, so gains are modelled on the gross amount only as an upper bound.
flagged.action: Reconstruct acquisition dates, RMB amounts and the exchange rate on each date.

flagged.title: Prior US filing compliance cannot be assessed
flagged.detail: If FBAR or Form 8938 obligations were missed in earlier years, the penalty exposure may dwarf every fee discussed here, and it cannot be quantified without the account history.
flagged.action: Check filing history for every year the account exceeded the thresholds before moving a large balance.

flagged.title: Whether original exchange memos exist and are within 24 months
flagged.detail: The exchange-memo route is the only one that needs no tax certificate at all, but it is limited to RMB that came from a prior conversion and expires after 24 months.
flagged.action: Search bank records for 原兑换水单 before treating this route as available.

flagged.title: PRC cash-carry declaration limits
flagged.detail: The GACC passenger-guide limits are cited from a prior session and were not re-fetched here, so no cash-carry figure is stated on this site. The US side (over USD 10,000 on FinCEN Form 105) is verified.
flagged.action: Read the current GACC passenger guide and the airline/customs rules before carrying cash.

flagged.title: One exchange rate is used throughout
flagged.detail: All RMB thresholds are converted at the PBOC central parity of 2026-11-06 (USD 1 = CNY 6.7168). The rate changes daily, and IIT Law Art. 16 requires foreign-currency income to be converted at the central parity rate on the relevant date.
flagged.action: Re-run the arithmetic with the central parity for the date that actually applies.

flagged.title: State tax, local tax and future law changes are out of scope
flagged.detail: The model covers US federal tax only. State income tax, the Netherlands or other residence-country rules, and any change in PRC or US law after 2026-11-08 are not modelled.
flagged.action: Add your state's treatment before relying on a net figure.

flagged.title: No other income, single filer, standard deduction
flagged.detail: The US residual column assumes a single filer with no other income and the 2026 standard deduction of $16,100. Real returns stack this income on top of other income, which usually raises the US rate and can change the residual.
flagged.action: Ask a preparer to run your actual return with and without the conversion.

flagged.title: Form 3520 penalty percentages
flagged.detail: The Form 3520 instructions contain a penalties section, but the percentages were not extracted in this session, so none are stated. An earlier portal attributed the 35% trust penalty (§6677) to foreign gifts generally, which is a mislabel: gifts fall under §6039F(c).
flagged.action: Read the current instructions for the penalty that applies to the specific part of the form.

flagged.title: Crypto prohibition and outbound-payment tax filing threshold
flagged.detail: The virtual-currency prohibition (S21) and the USD 50,000 outbound-payment tax filing threshold (S19) are cited from prior sessions and were not re-fetched here. They are described, not quantified.
flagged.action: Read the linked notices directly before acting.

flagged.title: Three separate dashboards disagreed with each other
flagged.detail: Earlier sessions published docs/, site/ and portal/ as parallel dashboards with different route counts (18 entries in data/methods.json versus 22 in portal/ and research/), two executive summaries, and incompatible source standards (one cited commercial bank and fintech pages). See the audit page for the row-by-row review.
flagged.action: This dashboard is now the entry point; the three earlier dossiers are preserved unchanged under their original paths.

flagged.title: Earlier entries mischaracterised §988 and Form 3520
flagged.detail: data/methods.json stated that a personal FX gain above $200 is reported as capital gain; §988(a)(1)(A) makes it ordinary. portal/ applied the §6677 trust penalty to foreign gifts generally; gifts are reported under §6039F. Both are corrected here and flagged for review.
flagged.action: Do not rely on those two earlier statements.
